    subcontractor_open_basis: Decimal
    confirmed_payroll: Decimal
    classified_payroll: Decimal
    difference: Decimal
    employee_reconciled: bool
    subcontractor_reconciled: bool

    @property
    def reconciled(self):
        return self.employee_reconciled and self.subcontractor_reconciled and self.difference == 0


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ProcessingResult:
    inputs: Inputs | None = None
    period: AuditPeriod | None = None
    receipts: ReceiptSummary | None = None
    register: tuple[PayrollRecord, ...] = ()
    decisions: dict[str, Decision] = field(default_factory=dict)
    allocation: AllocationResult | None = None
    adjustments: AdjustmentResult | None = None
    by_code: dict[str, Decimal] = field(default_factory=dict)
    application: ApplicationComparison | None = None
    independent_reconciliation: Reconciliation | None = None
    open_items: tuple[OpenItem, ...] = ()
    proposals: dict[str, ClassificationProposal] = field(default_factory=dict)
    site_visits: dict[str, tuple[date, ...]] = field(default_factory=dict)
    roofing_days: dict[str, tuple[date, ...]] = field(default_factory=dict)
    governing_field: GoverningFieldEvidence | None = None
    employee_comparisons: dict[str, EmployeeClassComparison] = field(default_factory=dict)
    unassigned_site_records: tuple[SourceReference, ...] = ()
    owner_assessment: OwnerAssessment | None = None
    combined_reconciliation: CombinedPayrollReconciliation | None = None


_PERIOD = re.compile(r"\bAudit period\s+([A-Z][a-z]+ \d{1,2}, \d{4}) to ([A-Z][a-z]+ \d{1,2}, \d{4})\b", re.I)
_RESTAURANT_POSITION = re.compile(r"(?:sous chef|chef|(?:line|prep) cook|cook|server|host|dishwasher)", re.I)
_CATERING_POSITION = re.compile(r"(?:catering|event)\b", re.I)
_GUIDE_WORDING = {
    "CG-02": "**CG-02. Assigning codes.** An employer is assigned the class code that describes its principal business. An employee whose work is described by another code in this guide is reported under that code. An employer may carry several codes.",
    "CG-41": "**CG-41. F-710 Restaurants.** Preparation and service of meals: kitchen staff, servers, hosts and dishwashers.",
    "CG-07": "**CG-07. Division of payroll.** When an employee performs work in more than one classification and the employer keeps records of the time spent in each, the employee's payroll may be divided between the codes.",
    "CG-42": "**CG-42. F-720 Off-site caterers.** Preparation of food and its service at events away from the employer's premises, including the catering crew of an employer that also runs a restaurant.",
}


def _source(document, locator):
    return _reference(document, 0, len(document.text), locator)


def _adjustment_evidence(document):
    monetary_columns = set(document.columns) & {"travel_allowance_paid", "amount_paid"} if isinstance(document, CSVSource) else set()
    return bool(monetary_columns or re.search(r"subcontract|certificate|travel|allowance", document.path.stem, re.I))


def _pending(reason, sources=(), rule_sources=()):
    return Decision("employer_evidence", "OPEN", None, None, reason,
                    (f"Auditor or employer must confirm: {reason}",),
                    tuple(rule_sources), tuple(sources), ("documented actual duties and audit period",), "whole_audit_period")


def _period(document, issues):
    if document is not None:
        matches = _PERIOD.findall(document.text)
        if len(matches) == 1:
            try:
                start, end = (datetime.strptime(value, "%B %d, %Y").date() for value in matches[0])
                if start <= end:
                    return AuditPeriod(start, end)
            except ValueError:
                pass
    issues.append(OpenItem("Audit period", "An unambiguous valid audit period is missing from the business description.", "Supply the authoritative start and end dates.", (() if document is None else (_source(document, "business description"),))))
    return None


def _receipts(table, period, issues):
    if table is None:
        return None
    refs = (_source(table, "monthly gross receipts"),)
    needed = {"month", "dine_in_receipts", "offsite_catering_receipts"}
    if not needed.issubset(table.columns):
        issues.append(OpenItem("Gross receipts", "Required monthly receipt columns are missing.", "Provide month, dine_in_receipts and offsite_catering_receipts.", refs))
        return None
    dine = offsite = 0
    months = []
    valid = bool(table.rows)
    for row in table.rows:
        month = row.values["month"]
        try:
            parsed = datetime.strptime(month, "%Y-%m").date()
            if parsed.strftime("%Y-%m") != month or month in months:
                valid = False
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            valid = False
        a = _cents(row.values["dine_in_receipts"], f"{table.path}:{row.line_number}")
        b = _cents(row.values["offsite_catering_receipts"], f"{table.path}:{row.line_number}")
        valid = valid and a >= 0 and b >= 0
        dine += a
        offsite += b
        months.append(month)
    total = dine + offsite
    percentage = None
    if valid and total > 0:
        with localcontext() as context:
            context.prec = max(50, len(str(abs(total))) + len(str(abs(offsite))) + 10)
            percentage = Decimal(offsite) * Decimal(100) / Decimal(total)
    else:
        valid = False
        issues.append(OpenItem("Gross receipts", "Empty, duplicate, invalid-month, negative or nonpositive-total receipts cannot verify the catering threshold.", "Provide a consistent, nonduplicated receipt summary.", refs))
    expected = []
    if period is not None and period.start.day == 1 and period.end.day == calendar.monthrange(period.end.year, period.end.month)[1]:
        year, month = period.start.year, period.start.month
        while (year, month) <= (period.end.year, period.end.month):
            expected.append(f"{year:04d}-{month:02d}")
            year, month = (year + 1, 1) if month == 12 else (year, month + 1)
    covered = valid and bool(expected) and sorted(months) == expected
    if not covered:
        issues.append(OpenItem("Receipt audit-period coverage", "Monthly receipt labels do not establish the same complete audit period; partial-month boundaries or missing/duplicate months require confirmation.", "Supply receipts for the exact audited dates or authoritative evidence explaining the summary's period boundaries.", refs))
    return ReceiptSummary(_money(dine), _money(offsite), _money(total), percentage, tuple(months), covered, refs)


def _guide_refs(evaluator, identifiers):
    refs = tuple(ref for ref in evaluator.rule_sources["catering_receipts"] if ref.locator in identifiers)
    valid = all(sum(ref.locator == identifier for ref in refs) == 1 for identifier in identifiers)
    # The existing evaluator retains a following section heading in the source
    # excerpt. It is structural context, outside this paragraph's policy text.
    valid = valid and all(" ".join(re.split(r"(?m)^#{1,6}[ \t]+", ref.excerpt, maxsplit=1)[0].split()) == _GUIDE_WORDING.get(ref.locator) for ref in refs)
    return refs, valid


def _direct_restaurant(evaluator, evidence):
    refs, valid = _guide_refs(evaluator, ("CG-02", "CG-41"))
    valid = valid and "F-710" not in evaluator.code_errors
    if not valid:
        return _pending("The current guide does not uniquely retain verified CG-02/CG-41 restaurant definitions; obtain auditor review.", evidence, refs)
    return Decision("restaurant_actual_duties", "CLASSIFIED", "F-710", "CG-41",
                    "Restaurant business and kitchen/dining field observations corroborate this register role as preparation/service of meals under CG-02 and CG-41.", (), refs, evidence,
                    ("restaurant employer", "corroborated restaurant kitchen/dining duties", "whole audit-period register"), "whole_audit_period")


def _application(document, register, allocation, by_code, adjustment_open, issues):
    if document is None:
        return None
    reported = []
    offset = 0
    seen = set()
    in_table = False
    for line in document.text.splitlines(keepends=True):
        cells = [cell.strip() for cell in line.strip().strip("|").split("|")]
        is_table = line.lstrip().startswith("|")
        if is_table and cells[0].startswith("Class code"):
            in_table = True
        elif is_table and in_table and not all(re.fullmatch(r":?-{3,}:?", cell) for cell in cells):
            if len(cells) != 3 or not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Z]-\d+", cells[0]) or not re.fullmatch(r"\d+", cells[1]) or not re.fullmatch(r"\d+(?:\.\d{1,2})?", cells[2]) or cells[0] in seen:
                issues.append(OpenItem("Application", "Malformed or duplicated application class row.", "Confirm the original reported code, employee count and payroll table.", (_source(document, "application"),)))
                return None
            reported.append(ApplicationClass(cells[0], int(cells[1]), Decimal(cells[2]), _reference(document, offset, offset + len(line), f"application class {cells[0]}")))
            seen.add(cells[0])
        offset += len(line)
    if not reported:
        issues.append(OpenItem("Application", "No valid reported class/payroll rows were found.", "Provide the employer's payroll split.", (_source(document, "application"),)))
        return None
    application_cents = {row.class_code: _cents(row.payroll, "Application") for row in reported}
    report_total = sum(application_cents.values())
    register_total = sum(_cents(row.wages, "Register") for row in register)
    difference = register_total - report_total
    pending = _cents(allocation.reconciliation.unresolved_total, "Unresolved register payroll")
    deltas = {code: _money(_cents(by_code.get(code, Decimal("0")), "Verified payroll") - application_cents.get(code, 0)) for code in sorted(set(by_code) | set(application_cents))}
    definitive = not any(line.status == "OPEN" for line in allocation.lines) and not adjustment_open
    if difference or sum(row.employees for row in reported) != len(register):
        issues.append(OpenItem("Application/register comparison", "The application payroll total or employee count conflicts with the payroll register.", "Confirm and correct the application; retain register wages without altering them to force agreement.", tuple(row.source for row in reported)))
    if not definitive or any(value != 0 for value in deltas.values()):
        issues.append(OpenItem("Application/classification comparison", "The verified allocation differs from the application or contains OPEN payroll; class differences are provisional while payroll remains unresolved.", "Confirm the evidence-backed classification changes and resolve pending employee decisions; the application is not classification authority.", tuple(row.source for row in reported)))
    return ApplicationComparison(tuple(reported), _money(report_total), _money(register_total), _money(difference), deltas, _money(pending), definitive)


def process_employer(
    guide_path: str | Path, employer_path: str | Path, interview_path: str | Path, *,
    files: EmployerFiles = EmployerFiles(),
) -> ProcessingResult:
    """Reread authoritative paths; return calculations/evidence without writing files.

    Adapters handle corroborated restaurant, legal-office and contractor duties.
    Unsupported contexts and ambiguous/missing evidence are OPEN, never guessed.
    """
    issues = []
    try:
        inputs = read_inputs(guide_path, employer_path)
    except InputError as exc:
        return ProcessingResult(open_items=(OpenItem("Input sources", str(exc), "Supply readable, valid authoritative source documents."),))
    try:
        interview = read_markdown(interview_path)
        interview_errors = ()
    except InputError as exc:
        interview = None
        interview_errors = (str(exc),)
        issues.append(OpenItem("Interview", str(exc), "Provide the preserved authoritative interview for house rules."))
    documents = {str(doc.path.relative_to(inputs.records_root)): doc for doc in inputs.records}

    def get(filename, expected_type):
        document = documents.get(filename)
        if not isinstance(document, expected_type):
            issues.append(OpenItem(filename, f"Required evidence {inputs.records_root / filename} is missing or has the wrong format.", "Provide the authoritative source at the configured location."))
            return None
        return document

    business = get(files.business, MarkdownSource)
    notes = get(files.notes, MarkdownSource)
    payroll = get(files.payroll, CSVSource)
    application = get(files.application, MarkdownSource)
    legal_office = bool(business and re.search(r"\bis (?:an? )?(?:[a-z0-9-]+ )?law office\b", " ".join(business.text.lower().split())))
    contractor = bool(business and re.search(r"\b(?:replaces roofs|(?:installs|performs) (?:roofing|siding)|roofing and siding contractor)\b", " ".join(business.text.lower().split())))
    homebuilding = bool(business and re.search(r"\bbuilds single-family houses\b", " ".join(business.text.lower().split())))
    receipt_table = None if legal_office or contractor or homebuilding else get(files.receipts, CSVSource)
    period = _period(business, issues)
    receipts = _receipts(receipt_table, period, issues)
    if payroll is None:
        return ProcessingResult(inputs=inputs, period=period, receipts=receipts, open_items=tuple(issues))
    try:
        register = records_from_csv(payroll)
    except AllocationError as exc:
        issues.append(OpenItem("Payroll register", str(exc), "Correct the authoritative register; no payroll total is invented."))
        return ProcessingResult(inputs=inputs, period=period, receipts=receipts, open_items=tuple(issues))
    evaluator = RuleEvaluator(inputs.guide, interview, source_errors=interview_errors)
    if homebuilding:
        from homebuilding_processing import evaluate_homebuilding, combine_payroll
        from contractor_processing import compare_employee_application
        evaluated = evaluate_homebuilding(inputs, business, notes, get(files.site_signins, CSVSource), payroll,
            register, period, evaluator, get(files.subcontractor_payments, CSVSource),
            get(files.certificates, CSVSource), interview, interview_errors, files)
        issues.extend(evaluated.open_items)
        result = _finish(inputs, payroll, period, receipts, register, evaluated.decisions, issues, application, interview, interview_errors,
            proposals=evaluated.proposals, site_visits=evaluated.site_visits,
            adjustments=evaluated.adjustments, adapted_adjustment_sources=evaluated.adapted_sources)
        comparisons, comparison_issues = compare_employee_application(result)
        return replace(result, governing_field=evaluated.governing_field, owner_assessment=evaluated.owner,
            combined_reconciliation=combine_payroll(result) if evaluated.adjustments is not None else None,
            unassigned_site_records=evaluated.unassigned_site_records, employee_comparisons=comparisons,
            open_items=result.open_items + comparison_issues)
    if legal_office:
        # Lazy import keeps the small evidence adapter separate while sharing
        # the established workflow models and finalization calculations.
        from legal_office_processing import evaluate_legal_office
        log = get(files.site_signins, CSVSource)
        office = evaluate_legal_office(inputs, business, notes, log, payroll, register, period, evaluator, files)
        issues.extend(office.open_items)
        return _finish(inputs, payroll, period, receipts, register, office.decisions, issues, application, interview, interview_errors,
                       proposals=office.proposals, site_visits=office.site_visits)
    if contractor:
        from contractor_processing import evaluate_contractor, compare_employee_application
        crew = get(files.crew_timesheets, CSVSource)
        log = get(files.site_signins, CSVSource)
        evaluated = evaluate_contractor(inputs, business, notes, crew, log, payroll, register, period, evaluator, files)
        issues.extend(evaluated.open_items)
        result = _finish(inputs, payroll, period, receipts, register, evaluated.decisions, issues, application, interview, interview_errors,
                         site_visits=evaluated.site_visits)
        comparisons, comparison_issues = compare_employee_application(result)
        return replace(result, roofing_days=evaluated.roofing_days, governing_field=evaluated.governing_field,
                       employee_comparisons=comparisons, unassigned_site_records=evaluated.unassigned_site_records,
                       open_items=result.open_items + comparison_issues)
    business_text = business.text.lower() if business else ""
    notes_text = notes.text.lower() if notes else ""
    context_text = business_text + "\n" + notes_text
    context_refs = tuple(_source(doc, "business description" if doc is business else "auditor field notes") for doc in (business, notes) if doc is not None)
    mapped_names = {files.business, files.notes, files.payroll, files.application, files.receipts}
    unmapped = [doc for name, doc in documents.items() if name not in mapped_names and not _adjustment_evidence(doc)]
    extra_columns = set(payroll.columns) - {"employee_id", "name", "position", "wages_paid"}
    if unmapped or extra_columns:
        issues.append(OpenItem("Unmapped employer evidence", "Additional source files or payroll columns are outside this adapter's schema and may change actual-duty findings.", "Review and map the additional evidence before assigning employee codes.", tuple(_source(doc, "unmapped evidence") for doc in unmapped) + ((_source(payroll, "unmapped payroll columns"),) if extra_columns else ())))
    restaurant = bool(re.search(r"\bis (?:an? )?(?:\d+-seat )?restaurant\b|\bthis restaurant\b", business_text))
    dining_observed = "kitchen" in notes_text and "dining room" in notes_text
    mixed_observed = "catering" in notes_text and "prepare" in notes_text and "serve" in notes_text and "venue" in notes_text and "restaurant shifts" in notes_text
    # This narrow adapter does not interpret individual exceptions or alternative
    # occupations. Any such evidence requires review, rather than a title match.
    exception = bool(re.search(r"\b(?:actual duties|misleading|bookkeep\w*|clerical|office|driver|roof\w*|siding|landscap\w*|nurs\w*|parking)\b", notes_text))
    # Business descriptions may legitimately mention customers' office events or
    # an outside accountant. Explicit employee-duty exceptions still need review.
    exception = exception or bool(re.search(r"\b(?:actual duties|misleading|bookkeep\w*|clerical)\b", business_text))
    negated_duties = bool(re.search(r"\b(?:no|not|never|without|unconfirmed|unknown)\b[^.!?\n]{0,60}\b(?:kitchen|dining room|restaurant shifts|prepare|serve|meal preparation|duties)\b", context_text))
    negated_industry = bool(re.search(r"\b(?:no|not|never)\b[^.!?\n]{0,30}\brestaurant\b", business_text))
    context_conflict = exception or negated_duties or negated_industry or bool(unmapped) or bool(extra_columns)
    if context_conflict:
        issues.append(OpenItem("Duty evidence requires review", "The supplied prose contains negated observations, employee duty exceptions or other occupations outside this adapter's supported restaurant context.", "Review actual duties and resolve exceptions before assigning a code; titles do not override those statements.", context_refs))
    timesheets_present = any("timesheet" in Path(name).stem.lower() for name in documents)
    no_timesheets = bool(re.search(r"\bno (?:employee )?timesheets (?:are available|exist|were kept)\b", context_text))
    positive_timesheets = bool(re.search(r"(?:^|[.!?]\s+)\s*(?:employee )?timesheets (?:are|were) (?:available|kept|provided)\b|\b(?:we|employer) (?:has|have|keeps|kept) (?:employee )?timesheets\b", context_text, re.M))
    sheets = True if timesheets_present or positive_timesheets else False if no_timesheets else None
    has_catering = any(_CATERING_POSITION.match(str(row.values.get("position", ""))) for row in payroll.rows)
    if has_catering and sheets is not False:
        issues.append(OpenItem("Employee timesheets", "No record confirms that employee timesheets are unavailable, or timesheet records are present; the verified mixed-duty rule requires no employee timesheets.", "Confirm timesheet availability and provide records or an authoritative no-timesheets statement.", context_refs))
    if has_catering and (timesheets_present or positive_timesheets) and no_timesheets:
        issues.append(OpenItem("Conflicting timesheet evidence", "Field notes deny available timesheets but a source or another statement indicates timesheets exist.", "Resolve the conflicting evidence before applying the no-timesheets rule.", context_refs))
    decisions = {}
    for employee, row in zip(register, payroll.rows):
        evidence = (employee.source, *context_refs)
        position = str(row.values.get("position", ""))
        if period is None or not restaurant or business is None or notes is None or context_conflict:
            decision = _pending("Confirm this employee's actual duties, restaurant industry and exact audit period; this adapter has no rule for other contexts.", evidence)
        elif _CATERING_POSITION.match(position):
            facts = RuleFacts(employee.employee_id, "restaurant", "catering_crew", period.start, period.end,
                              complete=bool(receipts and receipts.coverage_confirmed),
                              evidence_sources=(*evidence, *(receipts.sources if receipts else ())),
                              mixed_catering_restaurant_duties=mixed_observed,
                              employee_timesheets_available=sheets,
                              total_gross_receipts=receipts.total if receipts else None,
                              offsite_catering_receipts=receipts.offsite if receipts else None)
            guide_refs, verified_guide = _guide_refs(evaluator, ("CG-02", "CG-07", "CG-41", "CG-42"))
            decision = evaluator.evaluate("catering_receipts", facts) if verified_guide else _pending("The current guide's catering definitions differ from verified CG-02/CG-07/CG-41/CG-42; obtain auditor review.", facts.evidence_sources, guide_refs)
        elif _RESTAURANT_POSITION.fullmatch(position) and dining_observed:
            decision = _direct_restaurant(evaluator, evidence)
        else:
            decision = _pending("Register title and supplied observations do not establish supported actual duties; obtain employee duty evidence or an applicable rule.", evidence)
        decisions[employee.employee_id] = decision
        if decision.status == "OPEN":
            issues.append(OpenItem(f"{employee.name} [{employee.employee_id}]", decision.reason, "; ".join(decision.required_confirmation), decision.evidence_sources + decision.rule_sources))
    return _finish(inputs, payroll, period, receipts, register, decisions, issues, application, interview, interview_errors)


def _finish(inputs, payroll, period, receipts, register, decisions, issues, application, interview, interview_errors, *, proposals=None, site_visits=None, adjustments=None, adapted_adjustment_sources=()):
    """Share the existing exact-cent allocation, comparison and reconciliation."""
    allocation = allocate_payroll(register, decisions)
    # Rebuild the register from the loaded raw rows, independently of emitted lines.
    independent = reconcile_payroll(records_from_csv(payroll), allocation.lines)
    if not independent.reconciled:
        raise AllocationError("Independent payroll reconciliation failed")
    adjuster = PayrollAdjuster(inputs.guide, interview, source_errors=interview_errors)
    # No monetary adjustment schema is adapted in this first restaurant path.
    # Use the existing component for the empty evidenced set and expose any
    # candidate documents as OPEN, without accepting unbound external claims.
    adjustments = adjustments if adjustments is not None else adjuster.evaluate_batch()
    for line in adjustments.lines:
        if line.status == "OPEN":
            issues.append(OpenItem(line.adjustment_id, line.reason, "; ".join(line.required_confirmation), line.evidence_sources + line.rule_sources))
    unadapted_adjustments = False
    for document in inputs.records:
        if _adjustment_evidence(document) and str(document.path) not in adapted_adjustment_sources:
            unadapted_adjustments = True
            issues.append(OpenItem("Unadapted adjustment evidence", f"{document.path} may contain adjustment evidence that has not been supplied as verified typed cases.", "Provide sourced subcontractor/travel cases before treating adjustment processing as complete.", (_source(document, "adjustment evidence"),)))
    cents = {code: _cents(amount, code) for code, amount in allocation.by_code.items()}
    for code, amount in adjustments.by_code.items():
        cents[code] = cents.get(code, 0) + _cents(amount, code)
    by_code = {code: _money(amount) for code, amount in sorted(cents.items())}
    comparison = _application(application, register, allocation, by_code, unadapted_adjustments or any(line.status == "OPEN" for line in adjustments.lines), issues)
    return ProcessingResult(inputs, period, receipts, register, decisions, allocation, adjustments, by_code, comparison, independent, tuple(issues), proposals or {}, site_visits or {})

# Homebuilding Processing Implementation Plan

**Goal:** Integrate source-bound general homebuilding, office-site rules and subcontractor adjustments while preserving all three existing employer paths.

**Design:** Add a narrow `homebuilding_processing.py` adapter and configurable payment/certificate filenames. Reuse the reader, evaluator office rule, allocator, existing adjustment component, application attribution and shared finalizer. The internal adapter reads every supplied payment/certificate row; no external unbound monetary-case API is introduced. Only `employer_processing.py` and its API documentation change among existing files.

**Employees and owner:** CG-02/CG-15 support corroborated construction duties; the roofing/siding 15-day rule is inapplicable to general homebuilding. Derive governing evidence from field wages and check that recorded competing subcontractor exposures cannot overturn it. Use confirmed/possible office visit bounds as in Bay Crest. Preserve the estimator OPEN where four matched visits plus an unattributed row can cross the threshold. Record documented owner election separately; never invent or subtract owner wages absent from the register. Contradictory owner register presence stays OPEN.

**Subcontractors:** Bind original payment amounts/invoices/work/dates and certificate names/dates to reader rows. Exact full-period certificates exclude payments. Missing coverage after examining the complete supplied inventory invokes the existing 60-percent component. Lexically related, differently named certificate candidates are attached solely for OPEN review, never identity or coverage acceptance. Counterfactual missing-coverage calculations may provide separate proposals; no guessed identity or proposal contributes verified money. General framing/drywall use CG-15, roofing CG-11. Missing inventories or malformed/duplicate monetary evidence cannot become a fabricated zero adjustment total.

**Accounting:** Reconcile employee wages independently, subcontractor payment basis independently, and confirmed payroll as register wages plus verified subcontractor additions. Keep unresolved employee classifications distinct from unresolved subcontractor payment basis. Class totals contain only verified assignments; proposed additions are separate. Missing critical monetary sources prevent a combined confirmation.

**Verification:** Synthetic fixtures cover full/expired/missing/mismatched certificates, dates/names/invoices, scope, owner evidence, four/five-day bounds, source completeness and exact cents. Actual data is checked through independent raw CSV sums. Preserve old result digests after removing only newly added empty fields. Protect 70 existing files by SHA-256; retain Entire capture and no Git writes or external actions.

- [ ] Add failing synthetic and actual-source integration tests.
- [ ] Implement the source-bound adapter, owner assessment, internal adjustment integration and combined reconciliation.
- [ ] Run the complete suite and a read-only independent review; resolve findings.
- [ ] Verify all actual rows/cents/references, previous result equality, protected files and Git status; report findings without final deliverables.

from dataclasses import replace
from decimal import Decimal, localcontext
import csv
import io
import os

import tempfile
import unittest

"""
NOTES = """# Auditor field notes
Office in a converted house; three houses under construction. The office manager, Manager One,
drives material and paperwork out to the sites and meets inspectors there; the owner calls it "running errands".
The estimator visits a site now and then to measure. The bookkeeper stays in the office.
Three subcontractors were paid in the period (framing, drywall and roofing). The owner says they are all insured; we
collected the certificates of insurance the owner could find.
"""
PAYROLL = """employee_id,name,position,wages_paid
H1,Field One,Carpenter,100.00
E1,Estimator One,Estimator,50.00
M1,Manager One,Office Manager,60.00
B1,Books One,Bookkeeper,40.00
"""
APPLICATION = """# Application
| Class code (employer's choice) | Employees | Payroll (USD) |
|---|---|---|
| H-420 | 1 | 100.00 |
| C-110 | 3 | 150.00 |
"""
PAYMENTS = """date,subcontractor,work,invoice,amount_paid
2025-03-01,FrameBuild Co.,framing,FRAME-1,50.00
2025-04-01,DryBuild,drywall,DRY-1,20.05
2025-05-01,RoofBuild,roofing,ROOF-1,30.00
"""
CERTIFICATES = """subcontractor,certificate_no,coverage_from,coverage_to
FrameBuild Co.,CERT-F,2025-01-01,2025-12-31

"""


class HomebuildingIntegrationTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.temp.cleanup)
        self.root = Path(self.temp.name)
        self.employer = self.root / "independent-homebuilding-inputs"
        self.employer.mkdir()
        self.guide = self.root / "guide.md"
        self.guide.write_text(GUIDE, encoding="utf-8")
        self.interview = self.root / "interview.md"
        self.interview.write_text(INTERVIEW, encoding="utf-8")
        for filename, text in {"business-description.md": BUSINESS, "field-notes.md": NOTES,
                               "payroll-register.csv": PAYROLL, "application.md": APPLICATION,
                               "subcontractor-payments.csv": PAYMENTS, "insurance-certificates.csv": CERTIFICATES}.items():
            (self.employer / filename).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        self.set_visits()

        self.assertEqual(result.governing_field.class_code, "H-420")

        self.assertEqual(result.adjustments.reconciliation.payroll_added, Decimal("12.03"))

        self.assertEqual(result.adjustments.reconciliation.unresolved_basis, Decimal("30.00"))
        self.assertTrue(result.combined_reconciliation.reconciled)

        self.assertEqual(line.certificates[0].subcontractor, "RoofBuild & Siding LLC")
        self.assertEqual(line.payroll_added, Decimal("0.00"))
        self.assertEqual(line.proposal.payroll_added, Decimal("18.00"))
        self.assertEqual(line.input_record.decision.class_code, "R-310")

    def test_exact_name_expired_certificate_adds_sixty_percent_even_before_lapse(self):

        result = self.run_homes()

        self.assertEqual(result.combined_reconciliation.confirmed_payroll, Decimal("280.03"))

        self.assertNotIn("R-310", self.run_homes().adjustments.by_code)

    def test_unrelated_missing_certificate_is_not_hidden_by_a_different_vendor_certificate(self):
        line = next(line for line in self.run_homes().adjustments.lines if line.adjustment_id == "DRY-1")
        self.assertEqual(line.status, "VERIFIED")
        self.assertEqual(line.class_code, "H-420")
        self.assertEqual(line.payroll_added, Decimal("12.03"))
        self.assertTrue(line.input_record.raw_record)
        self.assertTrue(any(ref.locator == "CG-06" for ref in line.rule_sources))

    def test_missing_inventory_is_unknown_not_a_documented_missing_certificate(self):
        (self.employer / "insurance-certificates.csv").unlink()
        result = self.run_homes()
        self.assertEqual(result.adjustments.reconciliation.payroll_added, Decimal("0.00"))
        self.assertEqual(result.adjustments.reconciliation.unresolved_basis, Decimal("100.05"))
        self.assertTrue(all(line.status == "OPEN" for line in result.adjustments.lines))

    def test_missing_payments_do_not_fabricate_a_confirmed_combined_total(self):
        (self.employer / "subcontractor-payments.csv").unlink()
        result = self.run_homes()
        self.assertIsNone(result.combined_reconciliation)
        self.assertTrue(result.open_items)

    def test_duplicate_invoice_is_a_source_error_without_a_partial_combined_total(self):
        path = self.employer / "subcontractor-payments.csv"
        path.write_text(PAYMENTS + PAYMENTS.splitlines()[1] + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        result = self.run_homes()
        self.assertIsNone(result.combined_reconciliation)
        self.assertTrue(any("duplicate" in item.reason.lower() for item in result.open_items))

    def test_unknown_subcontractor_work_and_missing_certificate_dates_stay_open(self):
        path = self.employer / "subcontractor-payments.csv"
        path.write_text(PAYMENTS.replace("DryBuild,drywall", "DryBuild,unknown work"), encoding="utf-8")
        result = self.run_homes()
        self.assertEqual(next(line for line in result.adjustments.lines if line.adjustment_id == "DRY-1").status, "OPEN")
        (self.employer / "insurance-certificates.csv").write_text(CERTIFICATES.replace("2025-12-31", ""), encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertEqual(next(line for line in self.run_homes().adjustments.lines if line.adjustment_id == "FRAME-1").status, "OPEN")

    def test_four_confirmed_visits_plus_an_unattributed_date_preserves_open_classification(self):
        self.set_visits(estimator=4)

        self.assertEqual(result.combined_reconciliation.classified_payroll, Decimal("212.03"))
        self.assertEqual(result.proposals["E1"].class_code, "C-110")

    def test_owner_exclusion_requires_the_documented_election_and_consistent_register(self):
        path = self.employer / "business-description.md"
        path.write_text(BUSINESS.replace("has filed an election of exclusion", "has not filed an election of exclusion"), encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertEqual(self.run_homes().owner_assessment.status, "OPEN")

        self.assertEqual(result.independent_reconciliation.register_total, Decimal("260.00"))
        self.assertEqual(result.decisions["OWN"].status, "OPEN")

        (self.employer / "subcontractor-payments.csv").write_text(PAYMENTS.replace("ROOF-1,30.00", "ROOF-1,1000.00"), encoding="utf-8")
        result = self.run_homes()
        self.assertIsNone(result.governing_field.class_code)
        self.assertEqual(result.decisions["M1"].status, "OPEN")

    def test_configurable_sources_reread_and_keep_low_precision_cents_exact(self):
        (self.employer / "subcontractor-payments.csv").rename(self.employer / "invoices.csv")

            guide_refs, verified_guide = _guide_refs(evaluator, ("CG-02", "CG-07", "CG-41", "CG-42"))
            decision = evaluator.evaluate("catering_receipts", facts) if verified_guide else _pending("The current guide's catering definitions differ from verified CG-02/CG-07/CG-41/CG-42; obtain auditor review.", facts.evidence_sources, guide_refs)

def _finish(inputs, payroll, period, receipts, register, decisions, issues, application, interview, interview_errors, *, proposals=None, site_visits=None, adjustments=None, adapted_adjustment_sources=()):
    """Share the existing exact-cent allocation, comparison and reconciliation."""
    allocation = allocate_payroll(register, decisions)
    # Rebuild the register from the loaded raw rows, independently of emitted lines.
    independent = reconcile_payroll(records_from_csv(payroll), allocation.lines)
    if not independent.reconciled:
        raise AllocationError("Independent payroll reconciliation failed")
    adjuster = PayrollAdjuster(inputs.guide, interview, source_errors=interview_errors)
    # No monetary adjustment schema is adapted in this first restaurant path.
    # Use the existing component for the empty evidenced set and expose any
    # candidate documents as OPEN, without accepting unbound external claims.
    adjustments = adjustments if adjustments is not None else adjuster.evaluate_batch()
    for line in adjustments.lines:
        if line.status == "OPEN":
            issues.append(OpenItem(line.adjustment_id, line.reason, "; ".join(line.required_confirmation), line.evidence_sources + line.rule_sources))
    unadapted_adjustments = False
    for document in inputs.records:
        if _adjustment_evidence(document) and str(document.path) not in adapted_adjustment_sources:
            unadapted_adjustments = True
            issues.append(OpenItem("Unadapted adjustment evidence", f"{document.path} may contain adjustment evidence that has not been supplied as verified typed cases.", "Provide sourced subcontractor/travel cases before treating adjustment processing as complete.", (_source(document, "adjustment evidence"),)))
    cents = {code: _cents(amount, code) for code, amount in allocation.by_code.items()}
    for code, amount in adjustments.by_code.items():
        cents[code] = cents.get(code, 0) + _cents(amount, code)
    by_code = {code: _money(amount) for code, amount in sorted(cents.items())}
    comparison = _application(application, register, allocation, by_code, unadapted_adjustments or any(line.status == "OPEN" for line in adjustments.lines), issues)

# Severn Homebuilders: auditor's field notes

Visit on 2026-07-16. Office in a converted house; three houses under construction. The office manager, Dana Whitcomb,
drives material and paperwork out to the sites and meets inspectors there; the owner calls it "running errands". The
estimator visits a site now and then to measure. The bookkeeper stays in the office.

Three subcontractors were paid in the period (framing, drywall and roofing). The owner says they are all insured; we
collected the certificates of insurance the owner could find.
# Classification guide excerpt

Linden Shore Mutual, workers' compensation, Maryland. Edition of July 2025. Internal use by underwriting and premium
audit.

This excerpt holds the general paragraphs and the class codes our current new-business employers fall under. Audit
files cite a paragraph by its identifier (CG-01, CG-02 and so on). A class code is cited by the paragraph that
describes it.

## General

**CG-01. Premium basis.** Premium is charged per USD 100 of payroll in each class code at the rate underwriting sets
for that code. Payroll is reported for the policy period being audited.

**CG-02. Assigning codes.** An employer is assigned the class code that describes its principal business. An employee
whose work is described by another code in this guide is reported under that code. An employer may carry several codes.

**CG-03. Payroll.** Payroll is the gross remuneration paid to employees for the period: wages, salaries, commissions
and bonuses. Expense reimbursements that the employer can document, such as travel and lodging costs, are not payroll.

**CG-05. Owners and executive officers.** An owner or executive officer who has filed an election of exclusion is not
counted. An owner who is included is counted under the code for the work the owner does.

**CG-06. Subcontractors.** Payments to a subcontractor who does not carry workers' compensation insurance for its own
workers may be treated as payroll of the employer, under the code for the work the subcontractor performed.

**CG-07. Division of payroll.** When an employee performs work in more than one classification and the employer keeps
records of the time spent in each, the employee's payroll may be divided between the codes.

## Class codes

**CG-04. C-110 Clerical office employees.** Employees whose duties are confined to an office: correspondence,
bookkeeping, dispatching by telephone or radio, drafting and estimating at a desk, and professional staff who work in
the office.

**CG-11. R-310 Roofing.** Installation, repair and removal of roofs and roof coverings on any building, including
work on scaffolds and ladders at the roof line.

**CG-12. R-320 Siding and gutters.** Installation and repair of exterior siding, gutters, downspouts and exterior trim
below the roof line. Roofing work is described by CG-11.

**CG-13. L-620 Landscaping and lawn care.** Lawn mowing, planting, mulching and the care of grounds.

**CG-15. H-420 Residential homebuilding.** Construction and remodeling of dwellings: framing, drywall, interior
finish, carpentry and general labor at the building site. Roofing work is described by CG-11 and electrical wiring
by CG-21.

**CG-21. E-510 Electrical wiring.** Installation and repair of electrical wiring and fixtures inside buildings,
including service connections.

**CG-22. M-830 Metal fabrication shop.** Cutting, bending and welding of sheet and structural metal in a shop.

**CG-31. T-610 Courier and delivery drivers.** Drivers of vans and light trucks delivering parcels and documents,
and helpers who ride on the delivery vehicles.

**CG-35. G-950 Parking garage attendants.** Parking and retrieving customer vehicles.

**CG-41. F-710 Restaurants.** Preparation and service of meals: kitchen staff, servers, hosts and dishwashers.

**CG-42. F-720 Off-site caterers.** Preparation of food and its service at events away from the employer's premises,
including the catering crew of an employer that also runs a restaurant.

**CG-51. N-910 Home health care.** Personal care and nursing services in clients' homes.

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from decimal import Decimal
import hashlib
import io
import re
from typing import Iterable, Mapping

from input_reader import CSVRow, CSVSource
from rule_evaluator import Decision, SourceReference


class AllocationError(ValueError):
    """Invalid money, duplicate payroll evidence, or unreconciled wage parts."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PayrollRecord:
    employee_id: str
    name: str
    wages: Decimal
    source: SourceReference
    raw_record: CSVRow | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PayrollPart:
    part_id: str
    employee_id: str
    wages: Decimal
    source: SourceReference
    scope: str = "whole_audit_period"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class WageAllocation:
    employee: PayrollRecord
    part: PayrollPart
    wages: Decimal
    status: str
    class_code: str | None
    rationale_ref: str | None
    decision: Decision | None
    reason: str
    required_confirmation: tuple[str, ...]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Reconciliation:
    register_total: Decimal
    allocated_total: Decimal
    unresolved_total: Decimal
    difference: Decimal
    employee_differences: dict[str, Decimal]
    part_differences: dict[str, Decimal]

    @property
    def reconciled(self) -> bool:
        return self.difference == 0 and all(value == 0 for value in (*self.employee_differences.values(), *self.part_differences.values()))


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AllocationResult:
    by_code: dict[str, Decimal]
    lines: tuple[WageAllocation, ...]
    reconciliation: Reconciliation


def _cents(value: Decimal, context: str) -> int:
    if not isinstance(value, Decimal) or not value.is_finite():
        raise AllocationError(f"{context}: wages must be a finite Decimal, got {value!r}")
    numerator, denominator = value.as_integer_ratio()
    cents, remainder = divmod(numerator * 100, denominator)
    if remainder:
        raise AllocationError(f"{context}: sub-cent wages {value!r}; no rounding policy is assumed")
    return cents


def _money(cents: int) -> Decimal:
    whole, fraction = divmod(abs(cents), 100)
    return Decimal(f"{'-' if cents < 0 else ''}{whole}.{fraction:02d}")


def _identifier(value: str, context: str) -> str:
    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value or value != value.strip():
        raise AllocationError(f"{context}: identifier must be a nonblank string without surrounding whitespace")
    return value


def _source_key(source: SourceReference) -> tuple:
    if not isinstance(source, SourceReference) or not isinstance(source.source, str) or not source.source.strip() or not isinstance(source.locator, str) or not source.locator.strip():
        raise AllocationError("Payroll evidence requires a source filename and record locator")
    return source.source, ("line", source.line_start) if source.line_start else ("locator", source.locator)


def _register(records: Iterable[PayrollRecord]) -> dict[str, PayrollRecord]:
    employees = {}
    sources = set()
    for record in records:
        employee = _identifier(record.employee_id, "Register employee")
        if employee in employees:
            raise AllocationError(f"{employee}: duplicate employee in payroll register")
        key = _source_key(record.source)
        if key in sources:
            raise AllocationError(f"{employee}: duplicate payroll register source record {key}")
        _cents(record.wages, f"{employee} at {record.source.source} {record.source.locator}")
        employees[employee] = record
        sources.add(key)
    return employees


def records_from_csv(
    table: CSVSource, *, employee_column: str = "employee_id",
    wages_column: str = "wages_paid", name_column: str = "name",
) -> tuple[PayrollRecord, ...]:
    """Adapt reader rows, selecting only base wages and retaining original evidence."""
    missing = {employee_column, wages_column}.difference(table.columns)
    if missing:
        raise AllocationError(f"{table.path}: missing required payroll columns: {', '.join(sorted(missing))}")
    text_lines = list(io.StringIO(table.text, newline=""))
    digest = hashlib.sha256(table.text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
    records = []
    for index, row in enumerate(table.rows):
        employee = _identifier(row.values.get(employee_column), f"{table.path}:{row.line_number}")
        wages = row.values.get(wages_column)
        _cents(wages, f"{employee} at {table.path}:{row.line_number} column {wages_column}")
        end = table.rows[index + 1].line_number - 1 if index + 1 < len(table.rows) else len(text_lines)

# Code Reviewer Prompt Template

Use this template when dispatching a code reviewer subagent.

**Purpose:** Review completed work against requirements and code quality standards before it cascades into more work.

```
Subagent (general-purpose):
  description: "Review code changes"
  prompt: |
    You are a Senior Code Reviewer with expertise in software architecture,
    design patterns, and best practices. Your job is to review completed work
    against its plan or requirements and identify issues before they cascade.

    ## What Was Implemented

    [DESCRIPTION]

    ## Requirements / Plan

    [PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS]

    ## Git Range to Review

    **Base:** [BASE_SHA]
    **Head:** [HEAD_SHA]

    ```bash
    git diff --stat [BASE_SHA]..[HEAD_SHA]
    git diff [BASE_SHA]..[HEAD_SHA]
    ```

    ## The spec is a vision document

    The spec says what the software must do. It does not enumerate every
    input, environment, or condition the software will meet. For behavior
    the spec is silent on, judge by what a reasonable person using this
    software would expect: a reasonable person's expectation is a
    requirement, and a spec's silence is not permission. Grade such
    findings by their effect on that person, not by whether the spec
    mentions the trigger.

    ## Declined to judge

    Before your verdict, list every behavior you considered and set aside
    as outside the plan or spec, one line each, with the reason. The
    executor rules on each line; nothing you set aside is dropped
    silently. An empty list means you set nothing aside.

    ## Read-Only Review

    Your review is read-only on this checkout. Do not mutate the working tree, the index, HEAD, or branch state in any way. Use tools like `git show`, `git diff`, and `git log` to inspect history. If you need a working copy of a different revision, check it out into a separate temporary directory (e.g. `git worktree add /tmp/review-[SHA] [SHA]`) — never move HEAD on this checkout.

    ## You Do Not Dispatch Subagents

    Do all of this review yourself. Never spawn a subagent to review part
    of the diff, and never spawn another reviewer for a second opinion.
    This process already provides every review seat the work gets; a
    reviewer you spawn duplicates one of them at full cost, and its
    verdict counts for nothing. If the diff feels too large for one
    pass, review it in passes yourself and say so in your report.

    ## What to Check

    **Plan alignment:**
    - Does the implementation match the plan / requirements?
    - Are deviations justified improvements, or problematic departures?
    - Is all planned functionality present?

    **Code quality:**
    - Clean separation of concerns?
    - Proper error handling?
    - Type safety where applicable?
    - DRY without premature abstraction?
    - Edge cases handled?

    **Architecture:**
    - Sound design decisions?
    - Reasonable scalability and performance?
    - Security concerns?
    - Integrates cleanly with surrounding code?

    **Testing:**
    - Tests verify real behavior, not mocks?
    - Edge cases covered?
    - Integration tests where they matter?
    - All tests passing?

    **Production readiness:**
    - Migration strategy if schema changed?
    - Backward compatibility considered?
    - Documentation complete?
    - No obvious bugs?

    ## Calibration

    Categorize issues by actual severity. Not everything is Critical.
    Acknowledge what was done well before listing issues — accurate praise
    helps the implementer trust the rest of the feedback.

    If you find significant deviations from the plan, flag them specifically
    so the implementer can confirm whether the deviation was intentional.
    If you find issues with the plan itself rather than the implementation,
    say so.

    ## Output Format

    ### Strengths
    [What's well done? Be specific.]

    ### Issues

    #### Critical (Must Fix)
    [Bugs, security issues, data loss risks, broken functionality]

    #### Important (Should Fix)
    [Architecture problems, missing features, poor error handling, test gaps]

    #### Minor (Nice to Have)
    [Code style, optimization opportunities, documentation polish]

    For each issue:
    - File:line reference
    - What's wrong
    - Why it matters
    - How to fix (if not obvious)

    ### Recommendations
    [Improvements for code quality, architecture, or process]

    ### Assessment

    **Ready to merge?** [Yes | No | With fixes]

    **Reasoning:** [1-2 sentence technical assessment]

    ## Critical Rules

    **DO:**
    - Categorize by actual severity
    - Be specific (file:line, not vague)
    - Explain WHY each issue matters
    - Acknowledge strengths
    - Give a clear verdict

    **DON'T:**
    - Say "looks good" without checking
    - Mark nitpicks as Critical
    - Give feedback on code you didn't actually read
    - Be vague ("improve error handling")
    - Avoid giving a clear verdict
```

**Placeholders:**
- `[DESCRIPTION]` — brief summary of what was built
- `[PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS]` — what it should do (plan file path, task text, or requirements)
- `[BASE_SHA]` — starting commit
- `[HEAD_SHA]` — ending commit

**Reviewer returns:** Strengths, Issues (Critical / Important / Minor), Recommendations, Assessment

    if not isinstance(value, Decimal) or not value.is_finite():
        raise AllocationError(f"{context}: wages must be a finite Decimal, got {value!r}")
    numerator, denominator = value.as_integer_ratio()
    cents, remainder = divmod(numerator * 100, denominator)
    if remainder:
        raise AllocationError(f"{context}: sub-cent wages {value!r}; no rounding policy is assumed")
    return cents

    whole, fraction = divmod(abs(cents), 100)
    return Decimal(f"{'-' if cents < 0 else ''}{whole}.{fraction:02d}")

    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value or value != value.strip():

# Code Reviewer Prompt Template

Use this template when dispatching a code reviewer subagent.

**Purpose:** Review completed work against requirements and code quality standards before it cascades into more work.

```
Subagent (general-purpose):
  description: "Review code changes"
  prompt: |
    You are a Senior Code Reviewer with expertise in software architecture,
    design patterns, and best practices. Your job is to review completed work
    against its plan or requirements and identify issues before they cascade.

    ## What Was Implemented

    [DESCRIPTION]

    ## Requirements / Plan

    [PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS]

    ## Git Range to Review

    **Base:** [BASE_SHA]
    **Head:** [HEAD_SHA]

    ```bash
    git diff --stat [BASE_SHA]..[HEAD_SHA]
    git diff [BASE_SHA]..[HEAD_SHA]
    ```

    ## The spec is a vision document

    The spec says what the software must do. It does not enumerate every
    input, environment, or condition the software will meet. For behavior
    the spec is silent on, judge by what a reasonable person using this
    software would expect: a reasonable person's expectation is a
    requirement, and a spec's silence is not permission. Grade such
    findings by their effect on that person, not by whether the spec
    mentions the trigger.

    ## Declined to judge

    Before your verdict, list every behavior you considered and set aside
    as outside the plan or spec, one line each, with the reason. The
    executor rules on each line; nothing you set aside is dropped
    silently. An empty list means you set nothing aside.

    ## Read-Only Review

    Your review is read-only on this checkout. Do not mutate the working tree, the index, HEAD, or branch state in any way. Use tools like `git show`, `git diff`, and `git log` to inspect history. If you need a working copy of a different revision, check it out into a separate temporary directory (e.g. `git worktree add /tmp/review-[SHA] [SHA]`) — never move HEAD on this checkout.

    ## You Do Not Dispatch Subagents

    Do all of this review yourself. Never spawn a subagent to review part
    of the diff, and never spawn another reviewer for a second opinion.
    This process already provides every review seat the work gets; a
    reviewer you spawn duplicates one of them at full cost, and its
    verdict counts for nothing. If the diff feels too large for one
    pass, review it in passes yourself and say so in your report.

    ## What to Check

    **Plan alignment:**
    - Does the implementation match the plan / requirements?
    - Are deviations justified improvements, or problematic departures?
    - Is all planned functionality present?

    **Code quality:**
    - Clean separation of concerns?
    - Proper error handling?
    - Type safety where applicable?
    - DRY without premature abstraction?
    - Edge cases handled?

    **Architecture:**
    - Sound design decisions?
    - Reasonable scalability and performance?
    - Security concerns?
    - Integrates cleanly with surrounding code?

    **Testing:**
    - Tests verify real behavior, not mocks?
    - Edge cases covered?
    - Integration tests where they matter?
    - All tests passing?

    **Production readiness:**
    - Migration strategy if schema changed?
    - Backward compatibility considered?
    - Documentation complete?
    - No obvious bugs?

    ## Calibration

    Categorize issues by actual severity. Not everything is Critical.
    Acknowledge what was done well before listing issues — accurate praise
    helps the implementer trust the rest of the feedback.

    If you find significant deviations from the plan, flag them specifically
    so the implementer can confirm whether the deviation was intentional.
    If you find issues with the plan itself rather than the implementation,
    say so.

    ## Output Format

    ### Strengths
    [What's well done? Be specific.]

    ### Issues

    #### Critical (Must Fix)
    [Bugs, security issues, data loss risks, broken functionality]

    #### Important (Should Fix)
    [Architecture problems, missing features, poor error handling, test gaps]

    #### Minor (Nice to Have)
    [Code style, optimization opportunities, documentation polish]

    For each issue:
    - File:line reference
    - What's wrong
    - Why it matters
    - How to fix (if not obvious)

    ### Recommendations
    [Improvements for code quality, architecture, or process]

    ### Assessment

    **Ready to merge?** [Yes | No | With fixes]

    **Reasoning:** [1-2 sentence technical assessment]

    ## Critical Rules

    **DO:**
    - Categorize by actual severity
    - Be specific (file:line, not vague)
    - Explain WHY each issue matters
    - Acknowledge strengths
    - Give a clear verdict

    **DON'T:**
    - Say "looks good" without checking
    - Mark nitpicks as Critical
    - Give feedback on code you didn't actually read
    - Be vague ("improve error handling")
    - Avoid giving a clear verdict
```

**Placeholders:**
- `[DESCRIPTION]` — brief summary of what was built
- `[PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS]` — what it should do (plan file path, task text, or requirements)
- `[BASE_SHA]` — starting commit
- `[HEAD_SHA]` — ending commit

**Reviewer returns:** Strengths, Issues (Critical / Important / Minor), Recommendations, Assessment

# Code Reviewer Prompt Template

Use this template when dispatching a code reviewer subagent.

**Purpose:** Review completed work against requirements and code quality standards before it cascades into more work.

```
Subagent (general-purpose):
  description: "Review code changes"
  prompt: |
    You are a Senior Code Reviewer with expertise in software architecture,
    design patterns, and best practices. Your job is to review completed work
    against its plan or requirements and identify issues before they cascade.

    ## What Was Implemented

    [DESCRIPTION]

    ## Requirements / Plan

    [PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS]

    ## Git Range to Review

    **Base:** [BASE_SHA]
    **Head:** [HEAD_SHA]

    ```bash
    git diff --stat [BASE_SHA]..[HEAD_SHA]
    git diff [BASE_SHA]..[HEAD_SHA]
    ```

    ## The spec is a vision document

    The spec says what the software must do. It does not enumerate every
    input, environment, or condition the software will meet. For behavior
    the spec is silent on, judge by what a reasonable person using this
    software would expect: a reasonable person's expectation is a
    requirement, and a spec's silence is not permission. Grade such
    findings by their effect on that person, not by whether the spec
    mentions the trigger.

    ## Declined to judge

    Before your verdict, list every behavior you considered and set aside
    as outside the plan or spec, one line each, with the reason. The
    executor rules on each line; nothing you set aside is dropped
    silently. An empty list means you set nothing aside.

    ## Read-Only Review

    Your review is read-only on this checkout. Do not mutate the working tree, the index, HEAD, or branch state in any way. Use tools like `git show`, `git diff`, and `git log` to inspect history. If you need a working copy of a different revision, check it out into a separate temporary directory (e.g. `git worktree add /tmp/review-[SHA] [SHA]`) — never move HEAD on this checkout.

    ## You Do Not Dispatch Subagents

    Do all of this review yourself. Never spawn a subagent to review part
    of the diff, and never spawn another reviewer for a second opinion.
    This process already provides every review seat the work gets; a
    reviewer you spawn duplicates one of them at full cost, and its
    verdict counts for nothing. If the diff feels too large for one
    pass, review it in passes yourself and say so in your report.

    ## What to Check

    **Plan alignment:**
    - Does the implementation match the plan / requirements?
    - Are deviations justified improvements, or problematic departures?
    - Is all planned functionality present?

    **Code quality:**
    - Clean separation of concerns?
    - Proper error handling?
    - Type safety where applicable?
    - DRY without premature abstraction?
    - Edge cases handled?

    **Architecture:**
    - Sound design decisions?
    - Reasonable scalability and performance?
    - Security concerns?
    - Integrates cleanly with surrounding code?

    **Testing:**
    - Tests verify real behavior, not mocks?
    - Edge cases covered?
    - Integration tests where they matter?
    - All tests passing?

    **Production readiness:**
    - Migration strategy if schema changed?
    - Backward compatibility considered?
    - Documentation complete?
    - No obvious bugs?

    ## Calibration

    Categorize issues by actual severity. Not everything is Critical.
    Acknowledge what was done well before listing issues — accurate praise
    helps the implementer trust the rest of the feedback.

    If you find significant deviations from the plan, flag them specifically
    so the implementer can confirm whether the deviation was intentional.
    If you find issues with the plan itself rather than the implementation,
    say so.

    ## Output Format

    ### Strengths
    [What's well done? Be specific.]

    ### Issues

    #### Critical (Must Fix)
    [Bugs, security issues, data loss risks, broken functionality]

    #### Important (Should Fix)
    [Architecture problems, missing features, poor error handling, test gaps]

    #### Minor (Nice to Have)
    [Code style, optimization opportunities, documentation polish]

    For each issue:
    - File:line reference
    - What's wrong
    - Why it matters
    - How to fix (if not obvious)

    ### Recommendations
    [Improvements for code quality, architecture, or process]

    ### Assessment

    **Ready to merge?** [Yes | No | With fixes]

    **Reasoning:** [1-2 sentence technical assessment]

    ## Critical Rules

    **DO:**
    - Categorize by actual severity
    - Be specific (file:line, not vague)
    - Explain WHY each issue matters
    - Acknowledge strengths
    - Give a clear verdict

    **DON'T:**
    - Say "looks good" without checking
    - Mark nitpicks as Critical
    - Give feedback on code you didn't actually read
    - Be vague ("improve error handling")
    - Avoid giving a clear verdict

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from decimal import Decimal
import hashlib
import io
import re
from typing import Iterable, Mapping

from input_reader import CSVRow, CSVSource
from rule_evaluator import Decision, SourceReference


class AllocationError(ValueError):
    """Invalid money, duplicate payroll evidence, or unreconciled wage parts."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PayrollRecord:
    employee_id: str
    name: str
    wages: Decimal
    source: SourceReference
    raw_record: CSVRow | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PayrollPart:
    part_id: str
    employee_id: str
    wages: Decimal
    source: SourceReference
    scope: str = "whole_audit_period"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class WageAllocation:
    employee: PayrollRecord
    part: PayrollPart
    wages: Decimal
    status: str
    class_code: str | None
    rationale_ref: str | None
    decision: Decision | None
    reason: str
    required_confirmation: tuple[str, ...]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Reconciliation:
    register_total: Decimal
    allocated_total: Decimal
    unresolved_total: Decimal
    difference: Decimal
    employee_differences: dict[str, Decimal]
    part_differences: dict[str, Decimal]

    @property
    def reconciled(self) -> bool:
        return self.difference == 0 and all(value == 0 for value in (*self.employee_differences.values(), *self.part_differences.values()))


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AllocationResult:
    by_code: dict[str, Decimal]
    lines: tuple[WageAllocation, ...]
    reconciliation: Reconciliation


def _cents(value: Decimal, context: str) -> int:
    if not isinstance(value, Decimal) or not value.is_finite():
        raise AllocationError(f"{context}: wages must be a finite Decimal, got {value!r}")
    numerator, denominator = value.as_integer_ratio()
    cents, remainder = divmod(numerator * 100, denominator)
    if remainder:
        raise AllocationError(f"{context}: sub-cent wages {value!r}; no rounding policy is assumed")
    return cents


def _money(cents: int) -> Decimal:
    whole, fraction = divmod(abs(cents), 100)
    return Decimal(f"{'-' if cents < 0 else ''}{whole}.{fraction:02d}")


def _identifier(value: str, context: str) -> str:
    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value or value != value.strip():
        raise AllocationError(f"{context}: identifier must be a nonblank string without surrounding whitespace")
    return value


def _source_key(source: SourceReference) -> tuple:
    if not isinstance(source, SourceReference) or not isinstance(source.source, str) or not source.source.strip() or not isinstance(source.locator, str) or not source.locator.strip():
        raise AllocationError("Payroll evidence requires a source filename and record locator")
    return source.source, ("line", source.line_start) if source.line_start else ("locator", source.locator)


def _register(records: Iterable[PayrollRecord]) -> dict[str, PayrollRecord]:
    employees = {}
    sources = set()
    for record in records:
        employee = _identifier(record.employee_id, "Register employee")
        if employee in employees:
            raise AllocationError(f"{employee}: duplicate employee in payroll register")
        key = _source_key(record.source)
        if key in sources:
            raise AllocationError(f"{employee}: duplicate payroll register source record {key}")
        _cents(record.wages, f"{employee} at {record.source.source} {record.source.locator}")
        employees[employee] = record
        sources.add(key)
    return employees


def records_from_csv(
    table: CSVSource, *, employee_column: str = "employee_id",
    wages_column: str = "wages_paid", name_column: str = "name",
) -> tuple[PayrollRecord, ...]:
    """Adapt reader rows, selecting only base wages and retaining original evidence."""
    missing = {employee_column, wages_column}.difference(table.columns)
    if missing:
        raise AllocationError(f"{table.path}: missing required payroll columns: {', '.join(sorted(missing))}")
    text_lines = list(io.StringIO(table.text, newline=""))
    digest = hashlib.sha256(table.text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
    records = []
    for index, row in enumerate(table.rows):
        employee = _identifier(row.values.get(employee_column), f"{table.path}:{row.line_number}")
        wages = row.values.get(wages_column)
        _cents(wages, f"{employee} at {table.path}:{row.line_number} column {wages_column}")
        end = table.rows[index + 1].line_number - 1 if index + 1 < len(table.rows) else len(text_lines)

Reviewed the adapter version with the new narrative guards. Actual Severn processing reproduces the required totals, keeps all eight payments, preserves original certificate identities, and separates proposals from verified money.

**Important findings**

1. **Empty tables become verified zero evidence.**  
   [homebuilding_processing.py:107](/home/maxg/ch03-premium-audit/skills/class-code-assistant/homebuilding_processing.py:107), [231](/home/maxg/ch03-premium-audit/skills/class-code-assistant/homebuilding_processing.py:231), [291](/home/maxg/ch03-premium-audit/skills/class-code-assistant/homebuilding_processing.py:291)
   
   In temporary copies of actual inputs:
   - Header-only payments produce zero subcontractor basis and confirmed combined payroll **461879.70**, despite notes documenting three paid subcontractors.
   - Header-only payroll produces a reconciled combined total **24693.39**, despite eight documented employees.
   - Header-only sign-ins classify both manager and estimator **C-110**, treating missing records as zero visits.

   Reject conflicting empty monetary sources as incomplete and suppress combined confirmation. Empty sign-ins cannot establish zero visits where documented visits exist.

2. **Plausible certificate mismatches can become verified missing coverage.**  
   [homebuilding_processing.py:99](/home/maxg/ch03-premium-audit/skills/class-code-assistant/homebuilding_processing.py:99), [134](/home/maxg/ch03-premium-audit/skills/class-code-assistant/homebuilding_processing.py:134)
   
   Changing only the certificate name to **Kent Island Roof & Siding LLC** bypasses prefix matching. All three roofing payments then become verified additions totaling **27567.39**, and combined payroll increases to **514140.48**. Broaden candidate retrieval conservatively while preserving the original names and OPEN identity treatment.

3. **Negated or conflicting source statements still authorize classifications and money.**  
   [homebuilding_processing.py:121](/home/maxg/ch03-premium-audit/skills/class-code-assistant/homebuilding_processing.py:121), [173](/home/maxg/ch03-premium-audit/skills/class-code-assistant/homebuilding_processing.py:173), [193](/home/maxg/ch03-premium-audit/skills/class-code-assistant/homebuilding_processing.py:193)
   
   Reproductions:
   - “have not collected the certificates of insurance the owner could find” still verifies **24693.39** of drywall additions.
   - Appending “Garrett Holm works exclusively on roofing throughout the audit period” leaves **66315.40** classified H-420.
   - Appending “Tidewater Drywall performed only roofing work during this audit period” leaves its additions verified H-420.
   - Replacing the construction observation with “no houses under construction” still passes corroboration.

   Require affirmative, uncontradicted evidence; unsupported exceptions should remain OPEN.

4. **Revoked owner election remains EXCLUDED.**  
   [homebuilding_processing.py:74](/home/maxg/ch03-premium-audit/skills/class-code-assistant/homebuilding_processing.py:74)
   
   Appending “The election of exclusion was revoked before the audit period began” leaves the owner EXCLUDED. Conflicting election evidence should make the assessment OPEN. No wages were improperly removed in this reproduction.

**Minor**

Office decisions should cite the whole sign-in source as well as individual rows. With no unmatched visitors, a zero-visit bookkeeper currently has no log citation supporting that absence.

**Declined to judge**

- Pending documentation updates, as requested.
- External insurance/legal policy correctness beyond the supplied guide and interview.
- Historical preservation hashes and previous-workflow digest comparisons; those were verified by the coordinating agent.

**Assessment: With fixes.** The actual-source calculations and accounting separation work. The reproduced evidence-validation failures need regression tests and corrections before acceptance. Findings were sent to the coordinating agent; its pending fixes have not been independently reverified here.

def process_employer(
    guide_path: str | Path, employer_path: str | Path, interview_path: str | Path, *,
    files: EmployerFiles = EmployerFiles(),
) -> ProcessingResult:
    """Reread authoritative paths; return calculations/evidence without writing files.

    Adapters handle corroborated restaurant, legal-office and contractor duties.
    Unsupported contexts and ambiguous/missing evidence are OPEN, never guessed.
    """
    issues = []
    try:
        inputs = read_inputs(guide_path, employer_path)
    except InputError as exc:
        return ProcessingResult(open_items=(OpenItem("Input sources", str(exc), "Supply readable, valid authoritative source documents."),))
    try:
        interview = read_markdown(interview_path)
        interview_errors = ()
    except InputError as exc:
        interview = None
        interview_errors = (str(exc),)
        issues.append(OpenItem("Interview", str(exc), "Provide the preserved authoritative interview for house rules."))
    documents = {str(doc.path.relative_to(inputs.records_root)): doc for doc in inputs.records}

    def get(filename, expected_type):
        document = documents.get(filename)
        if not isinstance(document, expected_type):
            issues.append(OpenItem(filename, f"Required evidence {inputs.records_root / filename} is missing or has the wrong format.", "Provide the authoritative source at the configured location."))
            return None
        return document

    business = get(files.business, MarkdownSource)
    notes = get(files.notes, MarkdownSource)
    payroll = get(files.payroll, CSVSource)
    application = get(files.application, MarkdownSource)
    legal_office = bool(business and re.search(r"\bis (?:an? )?(?:[a-z0-9-]+ )?law office\b", " ".join(business.text.lower().split())))
    contractor = bool(business and re.search(r"\b(?:replaces roofs|(?:installs|performs) (?:roofing|siding)|roofing and siding contractor)\b", " ".join(business.text.lower().split())))
    homebuilding = bool(business and re.search(r"\bbuilds single-family houses\b", " ".join(business.text.lower().split())))
    receipt_table = None if legal_office or contractor or homebuilding else get(files.receipts, CSVSource)
    period = _period(business, issues)
    receipts = _receipts(receipt_table, period, issues)
    if payroll is None:
        return ProcessingResult(inputs=inputs, period=period, receipts=receipts, open_items=tuple(issues))
    try:
        register = records_from_csv(payroll)
    except AllocationError as exc:
        issues.append(OpenItem("Payroll register", str(exc), "Correct the authoritative register; no payroll total is invented."))
        return ProcessingResult(inputs=inputs, period=period, receipts=receipts, open_items=tuple(issues))
    evaluator = RuleEvaluator(inputs.guide, interview, source_errors=interview_errors)
    if homebuilding:
        if not register:
            issues.append(OpenItem("Payroll register", "The empty payroll register cannot substantiate the documented homebuilding employees.",
                "Supply the complete original payroll register before confirming employee or combined payroll totals.", (_source(payroll, "empty payroll register"),)))
            return ProcessingResult(inputs=inputs, period=period, open_items=tuple(issues))
        from homebuilding_processing import evaluate_homebuilding, combine_payroll
        from contractor_processing import compare_employee_application
        evaluated = evaluate_homebuilding(inputs, business, notes, get(files.site_signins, CSVSource), payroll,
            register, period, evaluator, get(files.subcontractor_payments, CSVSource),
            get(files.certificates, CSVSource), interview, interview_errors, files)
        issues.extend(evaluated.open_items)
        result = _finish(inputs, payroll, period, receipts, register, evaluated.decisions, issues, application, interview, interview_errors,
            proposals=evaluated.proposals, site_visits=evaluated.site_visits,
            adjustments=evaluated.adjustments, adapted_adjustment_sources=evaluated.adapted_sources)
        comparisons, comparison_issues = compare_employee_application(result)
        return replace(result, governing_field=evaluated.governing_field, owner_assessment=evaluated.owner,
            combined_reconciliation=combine_payroll(result) if evaluated.adjustments is not None else None,
            unassigned_site_records=evaluated.unassigned_site_records, employee_comparisons=comparisons,
            open_items=result.open_items + comparison_issues)
    if legal_office:
        # Lazy import keeps the small evidence adapter separate while sharing
        # the established workflow models and finalization calculations.
        from legal_office_processing import evaluate_legal_office
        log = get(files.site_signins, CSVSource)
        office = evaluate_legal_office(inputs, business, notes, log, payroll, register, period, evaluator, files)
        issues.extend(office.open_items)
        return _finish(inputs, payroll, period, receipts, register, office.decisions, issues, application, interview, interview_errors,
                       proposals=office.proposals, site_visits=office.site_visits)
    if contractor:
        from contractor_processing import evaluate_contractor, compare_employee_application
        crew = get(files.crew_timesheets, CSVSource)
        log = get(files.site_signins, CSVSource)
        evaluated = evaluate_contractor(inputs, business, notes, crew, log, payroll, register, period, evaluator, files)
        issues.extend(evaluated.open_items)
        result = _finish(inputs, payroll, period, receipts, register, evaluated.decisions, issues, application, interview, interview_errors,
                         site_visits=evaluated.site_visits)
        comparisons, comparison_issues = compare_employee_application(result)
        return replace(result, roofing_days=evaluated.roofing_days, governing_field=evaluated.governing_field,
                       employee_comparisons=comparisons, unassigned_site_records=evaluated.unassigned_site_records,
